exercise.name: Kettlebell One Arm Thruster

reference.title: Kettlebell One Arm Thruster
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time because the proxy blocked it, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip, knee, ankle, shoulder and elbow)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, squat down; breathe out as you drive up and press; breathe in again as the kettlebell come back to the shoulder.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s down, 1 s up and press, about 1 s back to the shoulder

prescription.tempo: Controlled squat, fast drive and press
prescription.progression: Heavier kettlebell, more reps per set, then timed sets for conditioning. Kettlebell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.
prescription.load: User-chosen kettlebell; one bell, both sides per set

cues.text: Feet about shoulder width, toes slightly out; kettlebell racked at the right shoulder (fist in front of the shoulder, elbow down and in), left arm out to the side.
Breathe in, brace and front squat until the hip crease is just below the knees; heels down.
Chest up, right elbow forward and down, knees out over the toes.
Drive the floor away; let the leg drive pop the kettlebell off the shoulder, then press straight up past the face.
Arm straight overhead, biceps by the ear, ribs down; breathe out.
Bring the kettlebell back to the shoulder before the next squat.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing before the legs have finished driving
mistakes.fix: Wait for the hips and knees to extend; the arms take over from the leg drive (CrossFit 2019).

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back at lockout
mistakes.fix: Brace the ribs down; finish with the kettlebell over the middle of the feet.

mistakes.mistake: Starting the next squat with the kettlebell still overhead
mistakes.fix: Bring it back to the shoulder first, then squat (CrossFit 2019).

mistakes.mistake: Racking elbow flaring out in the bottom
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow down and in so the bell stays on the forearm.

kinematics.norm: About shoulder width, toes slightly out (CrossFit 2019)
Hip crease just below the top of the knees at the bottom (CrossFit 2019)
Fairly upright under the front load (Gullett 2009); neutral spine (CrossFit 2019)

kinematics.setup: ≈19° in the rack (upper arm from vertical)
kinematics.norm: Arms fully extended overhead, the load stacked over the hips and ankles (CrossFit 2019)

kinematics.setup: Left arm out to the side, ≈43° from the body
kinematics.norm: Out to the side as a counterbalance (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Hand leaves the shoulder as the knees pass about 20° (0.15 s before full extension); lockout 0.4 s later
kinematics.norm: The press starts after the hips and knees have extended (CrossFit 2019)

kinematics.peak: 1.45 s down, 0.15 s bottom, 1.1 s drive and press, 0.4 s lockout, 1.1 s back to the shoulder
kinematics.norm: Controlled squat, fast drive and press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 21112, Kettlebell One Arm Thruster, video (movement reference)
CrossFit 2019, The Thruster (CrossFit Essentials, coaching article, 12 April 2019)
Gullett, Tillman, Gutierrez & Chow 2009, a biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals (J Strength Cond Res 23(1):284-292; PubMed 19002072)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a kettlebell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Clear space around and above you; do not lock out a kettlebell you cannot control overhead.
modify: Shoulder discomfort overhead: press to the forehead only or switch to a front squat.
Knee pain: squat to a box or a shallower depth.
regressions: Kettlebell front squat and a separate standing press.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Drive the squat out of the bottom; the leg drive pops the kettlebell off the shoulder (CrossFit 2019).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Drive the squat out of the bottom; the leg drive pops the kettlebell off the shoulder (CrossFit 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor out of the bottom of the front squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor out of the bottom of the front squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Presses the kettlebell overhead once the legs have extended (CrossFit 2019).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Presses the kettlebell overhead once the legs have extended (CrossFit 2019).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lifts the elbows up and out as the kettlebell pass the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lifts the elbows up and out as the kettlebell pass the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straighten the elbows to lock the kettlebell out overhead.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straighten the elbows to lock the kettlebell out overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Rotate and lift the shoulder blades so the arms can finish overhead; "shoulder drive up toward the bar" (CrossFit 2019).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Rotate and lift the shoulder blades so the arms can finish overhead; "shoulder drive up toward the bar" (CrossFit 2019).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blades upward at lockout (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blades upward at lockout (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Assist hip extension out of the deep squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Assist hip extension out of the deep squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and steady the knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and steady the knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Finish the leg drive and steady the shins (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Finish the leg drive and steady the shins (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk neutral in the squat and stops the low back arching at lockout (CrossFit 2019).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the chest up in the front squat under the front load (Gullett 2009).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the chest up in the front squat under the front load (Gullett 2009).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the kettlebell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Stop the trunk leaning away from the one-sided load; a unilateral press gave much higher external oblique activity than a bilateral press (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Stop the trunk leaning away from the one-sided load; a unilateral press gave much higher external oblique activity than a bilateral press (Saeterbakken 2012).
